notes:
First release. Mark a scene as a scaled battlefield and choose which combat distances scale with it — built for dragon battles, space combat, kaiju fights, and any map that represents far more ground than a five-foot grid.

A scaled scene keeps true-scale measurement — the ruler honestly reports the lair as 400 ft across — while the categories you pick keep their normal tabletop geometry. No combination of core scene settings gives you both.

How it works

Per category: ground covered = (base distance x multiplier) / scene grid distance.

With a 20 ft grid distance and a x4 multiplier, a 20 ft burst covers 20 ft of map — exactly the footprint it has on a normal scene. Leave movement unscaled and a 30 ft speed covers a quarter of its usual ground: the dragon owns the battlefield and the party cannot simply walk across it. That asymmetry is the point.

What is in it

  • Per-profile scaling categories, so spell areas can scale without movement, or the reverse.
  • Scaled Scene Wizard and a profile editor for setting scenes up.
  • Integrations for movement, attack ranges and melee reach, templates and areas, and vision and light.
  • Warns (without blocking) when a profile is assigned to a scene that still has a grid.

Requirements

  • Foundry VTT v13, dnd5e 5.x (verified against 5.2.5).
  • Scaled scenes should be gridless. On a rescaled square grid a 30 ft move lands on 1.5 squares, tokens snap wrong, and templates render as square-snapped approximations.
  • Scorpious187's Module Library is installed automatically as a dependency.

Full details in the release notes.
